sections.h2: What should a Mississippi home seller know about the state?
sections.html:
Mississippi is a state of about three million people, 82 counties, and a mostly owner-occupied housing stock. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page lists the numbers below, and they frame everything else in this directory.

MeasureFigure
Population estimate, July 1, 20252,954,160
Housing units, July 1, 20251,369,536
Owner-occupied housing unit rate, 2020 to 202470.0%
Median value of owner-occupied units, 2020 to 2024$169,800

Mississippi joined the Union on December 10, 1817 as the 20th state. Jackson is the capital and largest city, and Hinds is the largest county.

sections.h2: How is Mississippi laid out, and where do sellers cluster?
sections.html:
The state runs from river lowlands in the northwest to a Gulf shoreline in the south. Mississippi sits almost entirely within the east Gulf Coastal Plain, with lowland plains and low hills, and the northwest corner is the Mississippi Delta. The highest point is Woodall Mountain at 807 feet, near the Cumberland Plateau.

Common regional names are the Delta, the Golden Triangle, the Gulf Coast, the Natchez District, North Mississippi, the Pine Belt, and the Tennessee Valley. The main metro areas are Jackson, Gulfport-Biloxi, Hattiesburg, Pascagoula, and the Memphis, Tennessee area that reaches into the north.

Larger cities include Jackson, Gulfport, Southaven, Biloxi, Hattiesburg, Meridian, Olive Branch, Tupelo, and Greenville. Greater Jackson was the most populous metro area at 619,968 in the 2020 census.

sections.h2: What does the climate mean for a Mississippi house?
sections.html:
Mississippi has a humid subtropical climate, so heat, humidity, and storms are the main wear factors on a roof and structure. Late summer and fall bring the risk of hurricanes moving inland from the Gulf, especially in the south.

  • Hurricane Camille hit the coast on August 17, 1969 as a Category 5 storm.
  • Hurricane Katrina struck on August 29, 2005 and killed 238 people in the state. Both storms caused near total storm surge destruction of structures in and around Gulfport, Biloxi, and Pascagoula.
  • The state averages around 27 tornadoes a year, and two of the five deadliest tornadoes in U.S. history hit Natchez and Tupelo.

For a seller, storm history shows up in the roof, in flood and insurance questions, and in repairs a family may have put off. A buyer who purchases as-is does not ask you to fix any of it before closing.

sections.h2: How is property tax run in Mississippi?
sections.html:
Property tax is administered by local officials under rules set by the Legislature. The Department of Revenue explains that elected Tax Assessors, Tax Collectors, Chancery Clerks, Boards of Supervisors, city boards, and school boards all play a role, while the department oversees valuation and the State Auditor oversees collection.

Mississippi sorts property into five classes, each with a fixed assessment ratio.

ClassPropertyAssessment ratio
ISingle-family, owner-occupied residential real property10%
IIAll other real property except Class I or IV15%
IIIPersonal property other than motor vehicles15%
IVPublic utility property30%
VMotor vehicles30%

Tax equals true value times the assessment ratio times the millage rate. On the state's example, a $100,000 home at 10 percent and 125 mills owes $1,250. Real property must be revalued at least once every four years. All properties carry a county and a school district millage rate, and a city or special levee district adds its own.

sections.h2: What are the key property tax dates?
sections.html:
Mississippi assesses to the owner of record on January 1, bills in November and December, and collects by February 1. If February 1 falls on a weekend or legal holiday, payment is on time the following Monday.

  • January 1 to April 1: homestead exemption applications at the county Tax Assessor.
  • First Monday in August: normal deadline to request a hearing before the Board of Supervisors to contest a valuation.
  • February 1: taxes due for property assessed the preceding year.
  • First Monday in April or last Monday in August: county tax sale for delinquent real estate, depending on the county.

A property sold at a tax sale can be redeemed within two years under Section 27-45-3. Property not bought at the auction goes to the state and is managed by the Mississippi Secretary of State. Our statewide guides on the homestead exemption and estate and inheritance tax go deeper on each topic.

sections.h2: Where do deeds get recorded, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the chancery clerk of the county where the land sits. The Department of Revenue calls the chancery clerk the custodian of public land records, and assessors and tax collectors use those records to know who owns a parcel.

Fees are set by statute and published by county clerks. A fee schedule published by one county clerk, effective January 1, 2020 under Mississippi Code 25-7-9, shows warranty and quitclaim deeds at $26.00 in an archive-fee county and $25.00 in other counties, with each page beyond five adding $1.00. That schedule lists the counties that collect the $1.00 archive fee, so check which group yours falls into.

The same clerk's office states that handwritten documents are not accepted under an amended Section 89-5-24, so deeds must be typed. Clerks cannot give legal advice or search titles, so use a title company or attorney.

sections.h2: Who handles probate, foreclosure, and eviction questions?
sections.html:
Estates and many property disputes go through the county chancery court, and the clerk of that court keeps the files. One county clerk describes its role as handling matters of estates, guardianships, conservatorships, divorces, child custody, adoption, and property disputes.

Landlord and tenant cases follow a separate statute. The Residential Landlord and Tenant Act in Title 89, Chapter 8 requires written notice, a sworn affidavit or complaint, a court judgment, and a warrant carried out by the sheriff or a constable. See our guide to the Mississippi eviction process for notice periods and the 30 day hearing limit.

The state has no estate or inheritance tax on the Department of Revenue's account, so a family inheriting a house mostly deals with the chancery file, the deed, and the county tax bill.

sections.h2: What do sellers across Mississippi usually run into?
sections.html:
The most common friction points are paperwork and timing, not the sale price. Sellers in a Delta town, a Gulf Coast neighborhood, and a North Mississippi suburb all follow the same state rules, though the county offices differ.

  • Inherited houses with no recorded deed to the heirs.
  • Unpaid property tax that has moved toward a tax sale.
  • Storm damage and aging roofs, especially in the south.
  • Rented houses with a tenant in place or an eviction underway.
  • A homestead exemption that must be re-filed after a sale or a death.

This directory is general information. Rules and fees change, and each county office sets its own hours and payment methods. Confirm details with the county chancery clerk, Tax Assessor, or Tax Collector, or with a licensed attorney or tax professional.

faqs.q: How many counties does Mississippi have?
faqs.a: Mississippi has 82 counties. Each is divided into five districts, and voters in each district elect a supervisor to the county Board of Supervisors.

faqs.q: When are Mississippi property taxes due?
faqs.a: By February 1 for property assessed the preceding year. Property is assessed to the owner of record on January 1 and bills go out in November or December.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Mississippi?
faqs.a: With the chancery clerk in the county where the property is located. Fees are set by statute, and the clerk's office can tell you the current amount and format rules.

faqs.q: Does Mississippi have a state estate tax?
faqs.a: No. The Department of Revenue says no estate tax return is required for deaths on or after January 1, 2005, and the state has no inheritance tax or gift tax.

faqs.q: What is the largest city and county in Mississippi?
faqs.a: Jackson is the largest city and the capital, and Hinds County is the largest county. Greater Jackson is also the most populous metro area.
